description: Create, modify and delete RDS snapshots of DB clusters.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: copy_tags
parameters.description: Whether to copy all tags from source_db_cluster_snapshot_identifier to db_cluster_snapshot_identifier. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: db_cluster_identifier
parameters.description: The identifier of the DB cluster to create a snapshot for. Required when state=present.

parameters.name: db_cluster_snapshot_identifier
parameters.description: The identifier of the DB cluster snapshot.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: purge_tags
parameters.description: If purge_tags=true and tags is set, existing tags will be purged from the resource to match exactly what is defined by tags parameter. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified, even if purge_tags=True. Tag keys beginning with aws: are reserved by Amazon and can not be modified. As such they will be ignored for the purposes of the purge_tags parameter. See the Amazon documentation for more information https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html#tag-conventions. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: source_db_cluster_snapshot_identifier
parameters.description: The identifier of the DB cluster snapshot to copy. If the source snapshot is in the same AWS region as the copy, specify the snapshot’s identifier. If the source snapshot is in a different AWS region as the copy, specify the snapshot’s ARN.

parameters.name: source_region
parameters.description: The region that contains the snapshot to be copied.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Specify the desired state of the snapshot. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dictionary representing the tags to be applied to the resource. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Whether or not to wait for snapshot creation or deletion. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: wait_timeout
parameters.description: How long before wait gives up, in seconds. Default: 300

examples:
- name: Create a DB cluster snapshot
  amazon.aws.rds_cluster_snapshot:
    db_cluster_identifier: "{{ cluster_id }}"
    db_cluster_snapshot_identifier: new-cluster-snapshot

- name: Delete a DB cluster snapshot
  amazon.aws.rds_cluster_snapshot:
    db_cluster_snapshot_identifier: new-cluster-snapshot
    state: absent

- name: Copy snapshot from a different region and copy its tags
  amazon.aws.rds_cluster_snapshot:
    id: new-database-snapshot-copy
    region: us-east-1
    source_id: "{{ snapshot.db_snapshot_arn }}"
    source_region: us-east-2
    copy_tags: true

return_values.name: allocated_storage
return_values.description: The allocated storage size of the DB cluster snapshot in gibibytes (GiB). Returned: always Sample: 0

return_values.name: availability_zone
return_values.description: Availability zone of the database from which the snapshot was created. Returned: always Sample: "us-west-2a"

return_values.name: cluster_create_time
return_values.description: The time when the DB cluster was created, in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC). Returned: always Sample: "2024-07-01T05:27:53.478000+00:00"

return_values.name: db_cluster_identifier
return_values.description: Specifies the DB cluster identifier of the DB cluster that this DB cluster snapshot was created from. Returned: always Sample: "ansible-test-16638696"

return_values.name: db_cluster_snapshot_arn
return_values.description: Amazon Resource Name for the snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "arn:aws:rds:us-west-2:123456789012:snapshot:ansible-test-16638696-test-snapshot"

return_values.name: db_cluster_snapshot_identifier
return_values.description: Specifies the identifier for the DB cluster snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "ansible-test-16638696-test-snapshot"

return_values.name: engine
return_values.description: Specifies the name of the database engine for this DB cluster snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "aurora"

return_values.name: engine_mode
return_values.description: Provides the engine mode of the database engine for this DB cluster snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "5.6.mysql_aurora.1.22.5"

return_values.name: engine_version
return_values.description: Version of the cluster from which the snapshot was created. Returned: always Sample: "5.6.mysql_aurora.1.22.5"

return_values.name: iam_database_authentication_enabled
return_values.description: Whether IAM database authentication is enabled. Returned: always Sample: false

return_values.name: kms_key_id
return_values.description: The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. Returned: always

return_values.name: license_model
return_values.description: Provides the license model information for this DB cluster snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "general-public-license"

return_values.name: master_username
return_values.description: Provides the master username for this DB cluster snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "test"

return_values.name: percent_progress
return_values.description: Specifies the percentage of the estimated data that has been transferred. Returned: always Sample: 100

return_values.name: port
return_values.description: Port on which the database is listening. Returned: always Sample: 3306

return_values.name: snapshot_create_time
return_values.description: Provides the time when the snapshot was taken, in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC). Returned: always Sample: "2019-06-15T10:46:23.776000+00:00"

return_values.name: snapshot_type
return_values.description: How the snapshot was created (always manual for this module!). Returned: always Sample: "manual"

return_values.name: source_db_cluster_snapshot_arn
return_values.description: If the DB cluster snapshot was copied from a source DB cluster snapshot, the ARN for the source DB cluster snapshot, otherwise, null. Returned: always

return_values.name: status
return_values.description: Specifies the status of this DB cluster snapshot. Returned: always Sample: "available"

return_values.name: storage_encrypted
return_values.description: Specifies whether the DB cluster snapshot is encrypted. Returned: always Sample: false

return_values.name: tag_list
return_values.description: A list of tags. Returned: always Sample: [{"key": "tag_one", "value": "ansible-test-123456789012-rds-cluster-snapshot-b One"}]

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: Tags applied to the snapshot. Returned: always Sample: {"Tag Two": "two ansible-test-123456789012-rds-cluster-snapshot-b"}

return_values.name: vpc_id
return_values.description: ID of the VPC in which the DB lives. Returned: always Sample: "vpc-09ff232e222710ae0"
